seccomp_policy_enforced.title: Seccomp Policy Enforced
seccomp_policy_enforced.description: Indicates whether a seccomp profile is applied and enforced for the process or container, restricting allowable syscalls.

seccomp_profile_mode.title: Seccomp Profile Mode
seccomp_profile_mode.description: The mode of the seccomp filter applied: none means no filtering, strict allows only read/write/exit/_exit/sigreturn, filter applies a BPF-defined allowlist/denylist.

privileged_syscalls_accessible.title: Privileged Syscalls Accessible to Unprivileged Processes
privileged_syscalls_accessible.description: Indicates whether unprivileged processes can invoke privileged syscalls (e.g., ptrace, mount, kexec_load, perf_event_open) without restriction due to absent or permissive filtering.

ipc_mandatory_labeling_enforced.title: IPC Mandatory Labeling Enforced
ipc_mandatory_labeling_enforced.description: Whether a mandatory access control framework (e.g., SELinux, AppArmor, Smack) is configured to label and enforce policy on IPC channels including pipes, Unix domain sockets, and shared memory segments.

ipc_cross_trust_zone_channels_present.title: Cross-Trust-Zone IPC Channels Present
ipc_cross_trust_zone_channels_present.description: Whether IPC channels (pipes, Unix domain sockets, shared memory) exist between processes operating in different trust zones (e.g., unprivileged user processes communicating with privileged daemons).

ipc_input_sanitization_policy.title: IPC Input Sanitization Policy
ipc_input_sanitization_policy.description: The level of input validation and sanitization applied to data received over IPC channels by higher-trust zone processes before acting on it.

privileged_process_ipc_socket_permission.title: Privileged Process IPC Socket Permissions
privileged_process_ipc_socket_permission.description: The filesystem permission model applied to Unix domain sockets or named pipes exposed by privileged processes, indicating whether unprivileged processes can connect or write to them.

namespace_isolation_enabled.title: OS Namespace Isolation Enabled
namespace_isolation_enabled.description: Indicates whether processes are run with dedicated OS namespaces (PID, network, mount, IPC) isolating them from the host and adjacent processes. True means isolation is enforced; false means processes share the host namespace.

shared_namespaces.title: Shared Host Namespaces
shared_namespaces.description: List of namespace types explicitly shared with the host or adjacent trust zones (e.g., pid, network, ipc, mount, uts). An empty array means no namespaces are shared.

privileged_execution_mode.title: Privileged Execution Mode
privileged_execution_mode.description: Indicates whether the process or container runs in privileged mode, which disables namespace isolation and grants full host resource access.

credential_store_access_control_enforced.title: Credential Store Access Control Enforced
credential_store_access_control_enforced.description: Whether mandatory access controls (e.g., DAC/MAC permissions, LSM policies) are enforced on OS credential stores such as /proc memory maps, kernel keyrings, and LSA secrets, preventing unprivileged processes from reading them.

unprivileged_proc_mem_access_enabled.title: Unprivileged /proc Memory Access Enabled
unprivileged_proc_mem_access_enabled.description: Whether unprivileged users can read /proc/<pid>/mem or /proc/<pid>/maps of other processes (e.g., kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0 or equivalent permissive setting allowing cross-process memory inspection).

keyring_namespace_isolation_enabled.title: Kernel Keyring Namespace Isolation Enabled
keyring_namespace_isolation_enabled.description: Whether kernel keyrings are scoped to individual user/session namespaces rather than shared at the user or process-session level, preventing credential tokens in keyrings from being accessible to other processes in the same uid.

suid_sgid_binary_count.title: SUID/SGID Binary Count
suid_sgid_binary_count.description: Number of setuid or setgid binaries present on the filesystem outside of expected system paths (e.g., not in /usr/bin, /bin, /sbin).

suid_binary_argument_sanitization_enforc.title: SUID Binary Argument Sanitization Enforced
suid_binary_argument_sanitization_enforc.description: Whether custom or third-party SUID/SGID binaries are compiled with input validation and argument sanitization controls (e.g., use of secure_getenv, dropping privileges before processing user input, or wrapper scripts with strict allowlists).

suid_binary_integrity_verification_enabl.title: SUID/SGID Binary Integrity Verification Enabled
suid_binary_integrity_verification_enabl.description: Whether a file integrity monitoring or verified boot mechanism (e.g., IMA/EVM, AIDE, dm-verity) actively monitors and verifies the integrity of SUID/SGID binaries on the system.

nosuid_mount_coverage.title: nosuid Mount Option Coverage
nosuid_mount_coverage.description: Whether filesystems hosting user-writable or non-OS directories are mounted with the nosuid option, preventing SUID/SGID execution on those paths.

hidepid_mount_option.title: procfs hidepid Mount Option
hidepid_mount_option.description: The hidepid option set on the /proc filesystem mount, controlling which processes are visible to unprivileged users. 0=no restriction, 1=hides other users /proc/PID directories, 2=hides existence of other processes entirely.

unprivileged_container_proc_access.title: Unprivileged Containers Share Host procfs
unprivileged_container_proc_access.description: Whether unprivileged containers or processes can access the host /proc filesystem without a dedicated namespace or masking, exposing cross-trust-zone process metadata.

proc_gid_restriction_configured.title: procfs gid Restriction Configured
proc_gid_restriction_configured.description: Whether a gid= mount option is set on /proc to restrict access to a specific group, used in conjunction with hidepid=2 for finer-grained control.

cgroup_namespace_isolation_enabled.title: cgroup Namespace Isolation Enabled
cgroup_namespace_isolation_enabled.description: Whether processes in separate trust zones are placed in distinct cgroup namespaces, preventing cross-zone visibility of cgroup accounting data.

cgroup_accounting_readable_by_unprivileg.title: cgroup Accounting Files World-Readable by Unprivileged Processes
cgroup_accounting_readable_by_unprivileg.description: Whether cgroup resource accounting files (e.g., cpu.stat, memory.stat, blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes) under /sys/fs/cgroup are readable by unprivileged processes outside their own cgroup subtree.

privilege_transition_audit_enabled.title: Privilege Transition Audit Logging Enabled
privilege_transition_audit_enabled.description: Indicates whether the OS audit subsystem (e.g., auditd, Linux Audit Framework, Windows Event Auditing) is configured to log privilege escalation events such as setuid/setgid execution, capability grants, and sudo/su invocations.

namespace_crossing_audit_enabled.title: Namespace/Zone Crossing Audit Logging Enabled
namespace_crossing_audit_enabled.description: Indicates whether audit rules capture namespace transitions such as Linux namespace operations (clone, unshare, setns syscalls), chroot/pivot_root calls, and container breakout-related syscalls that represent zone boundary crossings.

ipc_syscall_audit_coverage.title: IPC and Syscall Audit Coverage Level
ipc_syscall_audit_coverage.description: Describes the breadth of audit rule coverage at the syscall/IPC layer for inter-process communication primitives that represent ingress/egress at zone boundaries (e.g., ptrace, process_vm_readv, mmap with PROT_EXEC, socket operations).

audit_log_integrity_protection.title: Audit Log Integrity Protection Enabled
audit_log_integrity_protection.description: Indicates whether audit logs are protected against tampering by unprivileged processes via real-time forwarding to a remote syslog/SIEM, write-once/append-only storage, or mandatory access controls preventing user-space modification.

capability_reset_on_exec_enforced.title: Capability Reset on exec() Enforced
capability_reset_on_exec_enforced.description: Indicates whether the process execution policy explicitly resets inheritable and ambient Linux capabilities (or Windows privileges) when spawning child processes via exec(), preventing capability propagation across the exec boundary.

no_new_privs_bit_set.title: no_new_privs Bit Set on Spawning Process
no_new_privs_bit_set.description: Indicates whether the PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit is set on the parent process before exec(), preventing child processes from gaining additional privileges through setuid binaries or capability-granting file attributes.

inheritable_capabilities_count.title: Number of Inheritable Capabilities on Parent Process
inheritable_capabilities_count.description: The count of Linux capabilities present in the inheritable capability set of the parent process that would be passed across exec() boundaries to child processes.

device_file_world_readable_writable.title: Device Files World-Readable or World-Writable
device_file_world_readable_writable.description: Indicates whether any character or block device files under /dev are accessible (read or write) by unprivileged users without group or ownership restrictions (e.g., permissions o+r or o+w on sensitive device nodes).

sensitive_device_nodes_with_open_acl.title: Sensitive Device Nodes with Open ACL
sensitive_device_nodes_with_open_acl.description: List of sensitive device node paths (e.g., /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, /dev/port, /dev/kvm) that have no restrictive ACL or udev rule limiting access to privileged groups or root only.

udev_device_acl_enforcement_enabled.title: Udev Device ACL Enforcement Enabled
udev_device_acl_enforcement_enabled.description: Indicates whether udev rules or equivalent device manager policies are configured and active to enforce group-based or ACL-based access restrictions on character and block device nodes, preventing unprivileged process access.
